Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware﴾. That is: He knows your outward forms, He knows your lineages, and He is aware of your inner selves; your secrets are not hidden from Him. So make taqwa your deed, and increase in taqwa as He has increased you.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 49, verse 14:

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey God and His Messenger, He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful."﴾

When God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, the most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you﴾, and the most righteous (al-atqa) is only so after taqwa (God-consciousness) has been attained, and the root of faith is guarding oneself against shirk, the Bedouins said: "We have noble lineage, and nobility belongs to us." God, exalted is He, said: Faith is not by speech; it is only by the heart. So you have not believed, for He is Knowing of what is in the breasts. ﴿But say, "We have submitted"﴾, meaning: we have yielded and surrendered. It was said: the verse was revealed concerning the tribe of Banu Asad, who displayed Islam in a year of drought, seeking charity, while their hearts were not reassured by faith. We have already explained that this is like the occasion of revelation (al-tarikh lil-nuzul), not a restriction to them, because everyone who displays the act of the God-conscious and wishes to attain what the pious attain of honor does not obtain that, since taqwa is an act of the heart.

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Say, "You have not believed"﴾, there are several issues in its explanation:

The first issue: God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not say to one who gives you greeting, "You are not a believer"﴾ [al-Nisa': 94]. Here He says: ﴿Say, "You have not believed"﴾, although they gave them greeting. We say: this is an indication that the work of the heart is not known, that avoiding suspicion is obligatory, and judgment is made only by the outward. So one is not said of one who does an act, "He is a show-off," nor of one who has become Muslim, "He is a hypocrite." But God is Knowing of what is in the breasts.

When someone says, "So-and-so is not a believer," certainty is established. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Say, "You have not believed"﴾, is what permitted us that statement, and it was a miracle for the Prophet ﷺ, since God informed him of the unseen and the inner state of their hearts. So He said to us: You should not say to one who gives you greeting, "You are not a believer," because you do not know what is in his heart.

The second issue: "lam" and "lamma" are both particles of negation, and "ma," "in," and "la" are likewise particles of negation. "Lam" and "lamma" apocopate (jazm) the verb, while the other particles of negation do not. What is the difference between them? We say: "lam" and "lamma" do to the verb what the others do not do, for they change its meaning from the future to the past. You say: lam yu'min amsi (he did not believe yesterday) and aman al-yawm (he believed today); you do not say: la yu'minu amsi. So when they did to the verb what no others among them do, they apocopated it. If it is said: despite this, why are they apocopating? The most that can be said is that the difference occurred; but what is the proof for the obligation of jazm with them? We say: because certainty and definiteness occur in past verbs; for whoever says qama (he stood), certainty of his standing is established, and it is not possible that he did not stand. Future verbs are either expected to occur or possible but not expected, and certainty and definiteness do not arise in them. So when "lam" and "lamma" convert the wording from future to past, they produce certainty and definiteness in meaning. Thus a correspondence was made between them in meaning, namely jazm, in wording. On this basis we say: the reason for jazm is what we mentioned. This is the case with the imperative, which apocopates, as if it were decisive regarding the one commanded that he will do it and not abandon it. What is the benefit that the wording is apocopated, when the act in it must occur, and in the conditional there is a change? That is because "in" changes the meaning of the verb from past to future, if it does not change it from future to past. You say: in ji'tani ji'tuka (if you come to me, I come to you), and in akramtani akramtuka (if you honor me, I honor you). Since "in" is like "lam" in being a particle, and in requiring that it enter upon verbs, and in changing the meaning of the verb, it became a jussive particle through verbal resemblance. As for the conditional response (jaza'), it is jussive for the meaning we mentioned, since the response is decisive upon its occurrence when the condition is present. So jazm is either for a meaning or for verbal resemblance, just as the response is likewise in the case of idafa and in the case of the genitive by a particle.

The third issue: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿But say﴾, requires a prior saying contrary to what follows it, like our saying: "Do not say, 'We have believed,' but say, 'We have submitted.'" In omitting explicit mention of it there is guidance and discipline. As if God, exalted is He, did not permit prohibiting their saying "We have believed," so He did not say, "Do not say, 'We have believed,'" and He guided them to refrain from lying, so He said: (You have not believed). If you are saying something, then say a general matter that does not entail your lying, like their saying: ﴿We have submitted﴾, for submission in the sense of yielding has occurred.

The fourth issue: the believer (mu'min) and the Muslim (muslim) are one according to the People of the Sunna. How is this understood with this? We say: there is a difference between the general and the specific. Faith is not realized except by the heart, though it may be realized by the tongue; Islam is more general. But the general in the form of the specific is united with the specific and is not another thing apart from it. Its example is that animal is more general than human; but animal in the form of human is not something separable from the human, and that animal cannot be an animal without being a human. So the general and the specific differ in generality but are united in existence. Likewise the believer and the Muslim. We will clarify this in the explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We brought out whoever was in it of the believers﴾ ﴿But We found not in it except one house of the Muslims﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 35–36], God willing.

The fifth issue: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾ — does it contain the meaning of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Say, "You have not believed"﴾? We say: yes, and its explanation is from several aspects. The first: when they said, "We have believed," and it was said to them, ﴿You have not believed; but say, "We have submitted,"﴾ they said: "If we have submitted, then we have believed." It was said: No, for faith is an act of the heart and not otherwise, while submission may be an act of the tongue. And when that is an act of the heart and faith has not entered your hearts, you have not believed.

The second: when they said, "We have believed," and it was said to them, "You have not believed," they said in dispute, "We have believed with sincere intention," affirming what they reported. So He said: ﴿And faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾, because "lamma yaf'al" is said in contrast to "qad fa'al" (he has done). It may also be said that the verse contains an indication to the state of those whose hearts are being reconciled (al-mu'allafa) when they become Muslim, and their faith is still weak; He said to them: ﴿You have not believed﴾, because faith is certainty, and that has not yet entered your hearts, and it will enter by your acquaintance with the excellences of Islam. ﴿And if you obey God and His Messenger﴾ — He will complete for you the reward. What indicates this is that "lamma" in it carries the meaning of expectation and anticipation. Faith is either by the believer's own act, acquisition, and reflection upon the proofs, or it is an inspiration that falls into the heart of the believer. So His saying, ﴿Say, "You have not believed"﴾, means: you have not done that. And His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾, means: nor has faith entered your hearts as inspiration without your act, so there is no faith for you at that time. Then, when they acted, He said, "You have not believed," with a particle that carries no meaning of expectation, because of the shortness of their view and the sluggishness of their thinking; and when they acted in faith, He said, "lamma yadkhul," with a particle carrying the meaning of expectation, because of the manifest strength of faith, as if it nearly covers the hearts entirely.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if you obey God and His Messenger, He will not deprive you﴾, meaning: He will not diminish you. The intent is that if you bring what befits your weakness of good deeds, He gives you what befits it of reward. This is because whoever brings to a king a good fruit whose price in the market is a dirham, and the king gives him a dirham or a dinar, attributes to the king little giving, rather stinginess. So its meaning is not that He gives the like of that without any reduction; rather the meaning is that He gives what you expect of your deeds without any reduction. In this there is encouragement toward sincere faith, because whoever performs an act without sincerity of intention, his work is lost and he is not given reward for it. So He said: ﴿And if you obey﴾ and are sincere, He will not diminish for you; so do not waste your deeds by lack of sincerity. In it also is consolation for the hearts of those whose faith came late, as if He says: Others preceded me and believed when the Prophet was alone, and sheltered him when he was weak; and we believed when we were unable to resist him and he overcame us with his strength. So our faith has no weight and we have no reward for it. Then God, exalted is He, said: Indeed your reward is not diminished, and what you expect you will be given. The most that can be said is that precedence increases their rewards. What harm is it to you if God is pleased to give others from the treasuries of His mercy a vast mercy? Your situation in that is only like that of a king who gave one man something and said to another: "What do you wish?" So he wished from him a vast city and wealth, and he gave him and fulfilled it, then added to the first man other things from his treasuries. If he is hurt by that, it would be stinginess and envy, and that does not occur in the Hereafter, and in this world it is a trait of the base. And His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ means: He forgives you what has passed and has mercy upon you for what you have brought.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then have not doubted and have striven with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. Those are the truthful.﴾

This is guidance for the Bedouins who said, "We have believed," toward the reality of faith. He said: If you want faith, then the believers are those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and then did not doubt, meaning they were certain that faith is certainty. The word "thumma" (ثُمَّ, then) here indicates delay in the narration, as if He were saying: they believed, then I say something else: they did not doubt. It may also be said that it indicates delay in the action, its meaning being: they believed in Allah and His Messenger, then they did not doubt what the Prophet (ﷺ) said about the gathering and the resurrection. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and have striven with their wealth and their lives﴾ confirms this, meaning: they were certain that after this abode there is another abode, so they strove seeking the final outcome. His saying, ﴿Those are the truthful﴾, means truthful in their faith, not the Bedouins who spoke words but did not sincerely act.

﴿Say: Do you inform Allah about your religion? And Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

He is Knowing of it and nothing is hidden from Him. This contains an indication that religion should be for Allah, while you have displayed it to us, not to Allah, so it will not be accepted from you.

﴿They consider it a favor to you that they have accepted Islam. Say: Do not consider your Islam a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred a favor upon you that He has guided you to faith, if you are truthful.﴾

This confirms that and clarifies that their Islam was not for Allah. In it there are subtle points:

The first: His saying, ﴿They consider it a favor to you﴾, is an added clarification of the ugliness of their action. That is because faith has two honors: one relating to Allah, exalted is He, which is declaring Allah free of polytheism and affirming His unity in greatness; and the second relating to the believer, for it purifies the soul from ignorance and adorns it with truth and sincerity. They therefore did not seek by their Islam the right of Allah, nor did they seek the honor of their own selves, but rather they showed favor. Had they known that it contained their honor, they would not have considered it a favor but would have given thanks.

The second subtle point: He said, ﴿Say: Do not consider your Islam a favor to me﴾, meaning: the Islam that you have is only in name; for this reason Allah, exalted is He, said, ﴿But say: We have submitted﴾, and He did not say: "You have not believed, but you have submitted," so that it would not become a confirmation of them in Islam as well, just as they were not truthful in faith. If it is said: why could it not be that they were truthful in their Islam, since Islam is submission, and it has been found from them in word and in deed, even if belief and knowledge were not found, and that amount suffices for their truthfulness? We say: denial occurs in two ways:

One of them: that the very thing reported about does not exist.

And the second: that it does not exist as it was reported in itself. One may say: "You did not bring us anything, rather need brought you," so Allah, exalted is He, denied them in their saying "We have believed" in the first way, meaning: you did not believe at all; and they were not truthful in Islam in the second way, for they submitted to need and to taking charity.

The third subtle point: He said, ﴿Rather, Allah has conferred a favor upon you﴾, meaning: you have no favor. And despite that, you do not submit in a straightforward exchange such that you have no favor over us nor we over you; rather the favor is upon you. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Rather, Allah has conferred a favor upon you﴾ is good manners, in that He did not say: "Do not consider it a favor to me, but to me is the favor upon you," in that He has shown you the straight path. Then, in response to this manner, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [Ash-Shura: 52].

The fourth subtle point: He did not say, "He has conferred a favor upon you that you have submitted," but rather He said, ﴿that He has guided you to faith﴾, because their Islam was misguidance, since it was hypocrisy, so He did not confer a favor by it upon them. If it is said: how did He confer a favor upon them with guidance to faith, when He had made clear that they had not believed? We say:

[Page 124]

The answer to this is from three aspects:

One of them: He, exalted is He, did not say, "Rather Allah has conferred a favor upon you that He has given you faith," but He said, ﴿that He has guided you to faith﴾, and the sending of the Messengers with the clear signs is guidance.

The second: He, exalted is He, confers a favor upon them according to what they claimed, as if He said: you said, "We have believed," and that is a blessing for you, since you have been saved from the Fire; so He said: "He has guided you" according to your claim.

The third, and it is the most sound: Allah, exalted is He, afterward stated a condition, saying: ﴿if you are truthful﴾.

The second: He, exalted is He, confers a favor upon them according to what they claimed, as if He said: you said, "We have believed," and that is a blessing for you, since you have been saved from the Fire; so He said: "He has guided you" according to your claim.

The third, and it is the most sound: Allah, exalted is He, afterward stated a condition, saying: ﴿if you are truthful﴾.

[Page 123]

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then have not doubted and have striven with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. Those are the truthful.﴾

This is guidance for the Bedouins who said, "We have believed," toward the reality of faith. He said: If you want faith, then the believers are those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and then did not doubt, meaning they were certain that faith is certainty. The word "thumma" (ثُمَّ, then) here indicates delay in the narration, as if He were saying: they believed, then I say something else: they did not doubt. It may also be said that it indicates delay in the action, its meaning being: they believed in Allah and His Messenger, then they did not doubt what the Prophet (ﷺ) said about the gathering and the resurrection. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and have striven with their wealth and their lives﴾ confirms this, meaning: they were certain that after this abode there is another abode, so they strove seeking the final outcome. His saying, ﴿Those are the truthful﴾, means truthful in their faith, not the Bedouins who spoke words but did not sincerely act.

﴿Say: Do you inform Allah about your religion? And Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

He is Knowing of it and nothing is hidden from Him. This contains an indication that religion should be for Allah, while you have displayed it to us, not to Allah, so it will not be accepted from you.

﴿They consider it a favor to you that they have accepted Islam. Say: Do not consider your Islam a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred a favor upon you that He has guided you to faith, if you are truthful.﴾

This confirms that and clarifies that their Islam was not for Allah. In it there are subtle points:

The first: His saying, ﴿They consider it a favor to you﴾, is an added clarification of the ugliness of their action. That is because faith has two honors: one relating to Allah, exalted is He, which is declaring Allah free of polytheism and affirming His unity in greatness; and the second relating to the believer, for it purifies the soul from ignorance and adorns it with truth and sincerity. They therefore did not seek by their Islam the right of Allah, nor did they seek the honor of their own selves, but rather they showed favor. Had they known that it contained their honor, they would not have considered it a favor but would have given thanks.

The second subtle point: He said, ﴿Say: Do not consider your Islam a favor to me﴾, meaning: the Islam that you have is only in name; for this reason Allah, exalted is He, said, ﴿But say: We have submitted﴾, and He did not say: "You have not believed, but you have submitted," so that it would not become a confirmation of them in Islam as well, just as they were not truthful in faith. If it is said: why could it not be that they were truthful in their Islam, since Islam is submission, and it has been found from them in word and in deed, even if belief and knowledge were not found, and that amount suffices for their truthfulness? We say: denial occurs in two ways:

One of them: that the very thing reported about does not exist.

And the second: that it does not exist as it was reported in itself. One may say: "You did not bring us anything, rather need brought you," so Allah, exalted is He, denied them in their saying "We have believed" in the first way, meaning: you did not believe at all; and they were not truthful in Islam in the second way, for they submitted to need and to taking charity.

The third subtle point: He said, ﴿Rather, Allah has conferred a favor upon you﴾, meaning: you have no favor. And despite that, you do not submit in a straightforward exchange such that you have no favor over us nor we over you; rather the favor is upon you. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Rather, Allah has conferred a favor upon you﴾ is good manners, in that He did not say: "Do not consider it a favor to me, but to me is the favor upon you," in that He has shown you the straight path. Then, in response to this manner, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [Ash-Shura: 52].

The fourth subtle point: He did not say, "He has conferred a favor upon you that you have submitted," but rather He said, ﴿that He has guided you to faith﴾, because their Islam was misguidance, since it was hypocrisy, so He did not confer a favor by it upon them. If it is said: how did He confer a favor upon them with guidance to faith, when He had made clear that they had not believed? We say:

[Page 124]

The answer to this is from three aspects:

One of them: He, exalted is He, did not say, "Rather Allah has conferred a favor upon you that He has given you faith," but He said, ﴿that He has guided you to faith﴾, and the sending of the Messengers with the clear signs is guidance.

The second: He, exalted is He, confers a favor upon them according to what they claimed, as if He said: you said, "We have believed," and that is a blessing for you, since you have been saved from the Fire; so He said: "He has guided you" according to your claim.

The third, and it is the most sound: Allah, exalted is He, afterward stated a condition, saying: ﴿if you are truthful﴾.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

This is an indication that your secrets are not hidden from Him, nor the hidden deeds of your hearts. And His saying ﴿Seeing of what you do﴾ means He sees the outward deeds of your limbs. The end of the surah, together with its connection to what precedes it, contains an affirmation of what is at the beginning of the surah, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger, and fear Allah﴾. For nothing is hidden from Him of what is secret, so do not neglect fearing Him in private, and nothing that is open is hidden from Him, so do not feel secure from Him in public. All praise is due to Allah alone, and blessings and peace be upon the one after whom there is no prophet (ﷺ).
